key_insight: SSH-Net improves competing-risks failure prediction by matching neural network substructures to distinct covariate groups and outputting cause-specific hazards.
engineering_relevance: The method is useful for reliability analysis of complex engineered systems, such as GPUs, where multiple failure causes and hierarchical inputs must be modeled together.
method: Build a structured segmented deep network with separate sub-networks for different covariate groups.
Use a cause-specific competing-risks formulation to predict cause-specific hazard functions.
Train with a penalized log-likelihood loss and derive cumulative incidence predictions.
evidence_signal: The paper validates SSH-Net using simulation studies and Titan GPU failure-time data, reporting Brier score, AUC, and RMSE for predicted cause-specific cumulative incidence functions.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful hyperparameter tuning and meaningful grouping of covariates, which can be challenging for complex systems.
paper_title: SSH-Net: A Deep Neural Network for Predicting Failure Time Distribution Functions under Competing Risks with Application to GPU Data
